title: Integers, powers and roots quiz
description: Ten questions drawn at random from a bank of fourteen, covering rational and irrational numbers, estimating roots and the index laws. No calculator.

questions.prompt: Select **every** irrational number in the list.
questions.explanation: $\pi$, $\sqrt{11}$ (11 is not square) and $\sqrt[3]{4}$ (4 is not a cube) are irrational. $\sqrt[3]{125} = 5$, $0.\dot{8} = \frac{8}{9}$, $6\frac{5}{11} = \frac{71}{11}$ and $\sqrt{4} = 2$ are all rational.

False. $\frac{22}{7} = 3.142857\dots$ is a handy approximation, but $\pi = 3.141592\dots$ They differ in the third decimal place. And $\frac{22}{7}$ is rational while $\pi$ is irrational, so they can never be equal.

questions.prompt: A rational number is always an integer.
questions.explanation: False. $\frac{1}{2}$ is rational but not an integer. It works the other way round: every integer is rational.

questions.prompt: Which is the best estimate of $\sqrt{20}$?
questions.explanation: $16 < 20 < 25$, so $4 < \sqrt{20} < 5$. 20 is nearly halfway between, so about $4.5$. (In fact $4.47\dots$) Option d halves 20 instead of square-rooting it.
$3^3 = 27$ and $4^3 = 64$, so the cube root is between 3 and 4. $3.5^3 = 42.9$ and $3.6^3 = 46.7$, so $\sqrt[3]{45} \approx 3.6$ (it is $3.56\dots$).

questions.prompt: Estimate the **positive** square root of 80 to 1 decimal place.
questions.explanation: $64 < 80 < 81$ and 80 is only 1 below 81, so $\sqrt{80}$ is just under 9: about $8.9$ (in fact $8.94\dots$).

questions.prompt: A square has an area of $30\ \text{cm}^2$. Estimate its side length to the nearest millimetre.
questions.explanation: Side $= \sqrt{30}$. $25 < 30 < 36$, so between 5 and 6. $5.4^2 = 29.16$ and $5.5^2 = 30.25$, and $30.25$ is nearer 30, so the side is about $5.5$ cm.

questions.prompt: Write each number as a power of 5 by typing the missing index.

questions.explanation: Same base, multiplying: add the powers. $-4 + 2 = -2$, so the answer is $7^{-2} = \frac{1}{49}$. Option b multiplied the powers instead.
Dividing: subtract the powers. $3 - (-5) = 3 + 5 = 8$, so $8^8$. Subtracting a negative is the step people slip on.
Power of a power: multiply. $2 \times -4 = -8$, so $(y^2)^{-4} = y^{-8} = \frac{1}{y^8}$.

questions.prompt: Match each decimal to the same number written as a power of 10.
questions.explanation: $0.001 = \frac{1}{1000} = \frac{1}{10^3} = 10^{-3}$. The negative power is the number of the decimal place the 1 sits in.

questions.prompt: A cube has a volume of $48\ \text{cm}^3$. Estimate its side length to the nearest millimetre.
questions.explanation: Side $= \sqrt[3]{48}$. $3^3 = 27$ and $4^3 = 64$. $3.6^3 = 46.7$ and $3.7^3 = 50.7$, so to the nearest millimetre the side is $3.6$ cm.
